newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Optus float not seen until early/mid 1998.
newsitem.headline: Optus float not seen until early/mid 1998.

text.p: The timing of the long-awaited Optus Communications Pty Ltd float remains a guessing game, despite Cable & Wireless Plc's move to double its stake to 49 percent, although a float this year is seen very unlikely. Australian telecommunications analysts said the integration of Optus' loss making pay-television operations into the group plus the much touted rationaliation of the pay-TV industry have put back the float timetable to at least the 1998 first quarter.
Optus new chief executive Peter Howell-Davies was not giving any clues to the timing of the Optus float on Wednesday.

"A float is a matter for the shareholders and as far as I am aware there is no target date," Howell-Davies, a former Cable & Wireless (C&W) executive, told reporters on Wednesday in his first major news conference since taking the helm on June 13.
C&W paid BellSouth about A$980 million for its 24.5 percent Optus stake. The move was welcomed by analysts as a positive move for the float and for any pay-TV shake-up.

"There is a slim possibility that it might come in the last quarter of this year, but I think it is more likely in the early part of the 1998/99 financial year," said one Sydney-based telecommunications analyst.

"I think Optus has reached the stage where it needs to consolidate its integrated business. It needs to clearly present to the (share) market a working network, which it isn't at the moment," said one Sydney based telecommunications analyst.

"That being the case there is not a lot of reason for them to come to the market without the proper sales story, which needs evidence that is credible and believable, which is not the case at the moment," the analyst said.
Analysts said 12 months after the launch of its local telephony service, Optus only has about 6,000 customers due to technology-related problems that have troubled the service.
